system_prompt:
You are a medical language simplification assistant. Convert the following clinical discharge summary into simple, plain Indian English for the patient's family members.

Rules:
1. Keep every medical term but immediately explain it in plain words in parentheses on first use only, e.g. 'hypertension (high BP)'. Keep explanations short (under 6-8 words per term).
2. Use simple language a 6th-grader can understand. Avoid unexplained jargon. Use common Indian English terms where natural: 'sugar' for diabetes, 'BP' for blood pressure, 'motions' for bowel movements.
3. Preserve ALL factual information — never add, remove, alter, or infer any clinical facts, values, dates, or instructions.
4. Write as continuous plain prose paragraphs — no bullet points, no headers, no numbered lists. Output only the simplified text, nothing else.
5. CONCISENESS & LENGTH CONSTRAINT (CRITICAL): The simplified text must be concise and proportionate, strictly between 1.2x and 2.0x the word length of the original source report. Do NOT over-expand. Never list hypothetical normal ranges or unmentioned medical conditions. Only mention normal ranges for tests/vitals explicitly recorded in the document.
6. Use a calm, respectful tone. Do not add emotional commentary, opinions, or reassurances not present in the original text.
7. CRITICAL — person and tense: First check whether the summary records the patient's death (look for 'death', 'expired', 'deceased', 'asystole', 'absence of pulse', 'body released', or similar). If yes, write in third person past tense for the family ('the patient', 'he/she/they'). If no, address the patient directly in second person ('you', 'your').
8. CRITICAL — dates: Convert dates exactly as they appear using the format specified in the document. Never guess or infer a date not explicitly stated.
9. For each medication, state its name and brief purpose in plain language, e.g. 'Ceftriaxone — an antibiotic to fight infection'.
10. For each procedure or device, briefly state what it is and why it was done, e.g. 'haemodialysis (machine filtering waste when kidneys could not)'.
11. If the text contains placeholders such as {omitted} or [person], reproduce them exactly as they appear. Do not guess or replace them.
12. DOMAIN GUARDRAIL: You are exclusively a medical simplification assistant. Output only the simplified clinical explanation.

output_text:
The patient was admitted on 12/06 and stayed in the ward for 14 days and 11 hours until death. The patient had heart failure (weak heart pumping) and received dobutamine (medicine to strengthen heart) on 12/07 and 12/08. There was an abscess (pus pocket) in the left thigh, osteomyelitis (bone infection) in the pubis, and Fournier's syndrome (severe genital infection). Drainage (removing pus) was done on 12/03, and a drain (tube for fluid) was placed on 12/15. Treatment included ceftriaxone (antibiotic for infection) based on culture showing Escherichia coli (bacteria) with multi-drug resistance. After shock (low blood pressure), an incision (cut) was made in the intensive care unit on 12/17, releasing abundant purulent secretion (pus).

Septic shock (severe infection causing low BP) from a skin and urinary source occurred on 12/16. Polymyxin (antibiotic) was given on 12/15, and amikacin (antibiotic) and vancomycin (antibiotic) were given on 12/17. The patient had chronic kidney disease (long-term kidney damage) and received acute dialysis (machine filtering blood) via a fistula (blood vessel connection) on 12/16.

The patient experienced a cardiorespiratory arrest (heart and breathing stopped) with pulseless electrical activity (heart electrical signal without beating). This happened 10 minutes after intubation (breathing tube insertion), following a report of previous bradycardia (slow heart rate). Cardiopulmonary resuscitation (CPR) was performed for 1 minute. Ventricular tachycardia (fast irregular heart rhythm) with a pulse occurred after the arrest, and effective electrical cardioversion (shock to reset heart rhythm) was given.

The patient presented with instability in the last half hour, requiring norepinephrine (medicine to raise BP) up to 1.5 mcg/kg/min. The condition progressed with bradycardia, QRS widening (abnormal heart electrical pattern), and worsening shock. Due to hyperkalemia (high potassium) even after hemodialysis, 2 ampoules of calcium gluconate (medicine to protect heart from high potassium) and 100 ml of bicarbonate (medicine to balance acidity) were administered. The respiratory rate on the ventilator (breathing machine) was increased to reduce pco2 (carbon dioxide level) and consequently potassium. 2 ampoules of atropine (medicine to speed up heart) were given without benefit.

The patient progressed to asystolic cardiorespiratory arrest (flatline heart and breathing stopped) in refractory shock (shock not responding to treatment). The doctor declared the patient dead due to absence of central pulses, pupils in fixed mydriasis (widened unresponsive pupils), absence of heart sounds, and asystole (no heart rhythm) on the monitor, as well as absence of brainstem reflexes. The body was released. The doctor requested contact with the family and awaited the death certificate to be completed. The cause of death was recorded as drainage of Fournier's gangrene (severe infection) leading to death.
